title: Stock arrangements and playing by head
summary: The band bought published orchestrations, especially Ted Lewis's, and played standards like High Society and Panama by head.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, did y'all have arrangements in that band, written arrangements? Yeah.
We played orchestration, and the biggest arrangement we had was Ted Lewis's arrangements. We used to play all the Ted Lewis arrangements.
Would you play those by head, or would you go out and buy them?

No, we'd play the music. A lot of music. All the numbers we'd play by head was like High Society, St. Louis, Panama Rang, you know, Tiger Rang, the regular... Yeah. Regular standards numbers. Regular standards numbers. Regular standards numbers. Shaking and breaking and all that kind of stuff.
But where would you get these arrangements? We'd buy them. Where?

The music store. The music store. The world line. See, they came in big arrangements, you know, like a big book. Uh-huh. Everybody's parts in it. Something like these, maybe I'd say like the light concert, you know? Uh-huh. We played all of them. Stanker Rang, which you'd buy them. Yeah. But especially Ted Lewis.
I wonder who did and who Rang did then. I can't remember.

I think most of them was Frank Skinner. I don't know who did, I don't think it was Frank Skinner. No. We had quite a few Frank Skinners there. I don't know who was Frank Skinner. I don't know who was Frank Skinner. Archie Bly and Frank Skinner. Yeah. That's the two... Archie Bly and Frank Skinner. Yeah. But I don't know who... Yeah. I don't know who they was off the top of it. Who they was the Rang for, you know? Uh-huh.
